criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of NSCLC with locally advanced, unresectable Stage IIIB or IIIC not eligible for definitive chemoradiotherapy or metastatic (Stage IV: M1a, M1b, or M1c) disease per the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) Staging Manual, Version 8.0, and the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) Staging System.
The participant has a neuroendocrine component or histology.
PD-L1 expression is on ≥1% of tumor cells based on local immunohistochemistry (IHC) testing with an assay utilizing the anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody clones 22C3 or SP263.
The participant has NSCLC with known AGAs.
The participant is able to provide tumor tissues for biomarker analysis.
The participant has an archival specimen (preferably collected within 12 months after the last anticancer therapy).
The participant has a de novo biopsy from a tumor lesion, if medically feasible.
The participant has received therapies and progressed during or relapsed after receiving their most recent prior therapy, or has been intolerant to their most recent therapy.
The participant has no known AGAs and fulfills 1 of the following conditions.

The participant received a platinum-based combination therapy for the treatment of metastatic or recurrent disease, and unless contraindicated, a PD-(L)1 monoclonal antibody (concurrently or sequentially with platinum-based chemotherapy).

The participant experienced disease progression within 6 months of the last dose of platinum-based chemotherapy in the adjuvant, neoadjuvant, or chemoradiotherapy setting and received a PD-(L)1 monoclonal antibody at any time during the course of treatment.
The participant has known AGAs (eg, EGFR mutations, ALK translocations, or other relevant actionable mutations) and fulfills the following conditions.

The participant has received at least 1 relevant AGA-targeted therapy if locally available and, in the opinion of the investigator, additional AGA-targeted therapy is not in the best interest of the participant.

The participant received a platinum-based combination therapy for the treatment of metastatic or recurrent disease, or experienced disease progression within 6 months of the last dose of platinum-based chemotherapy in the adjuvant, neoadjuvant, or chemoradiotherapy setting.
The participant may have received PD-(L)1 monoclonal antibody (concurrently or sequentially with platinum-based chemotherapy).
The participant has a history of another malignancy within 3 years before the first dose of PF-08046054, or any evidence of residual disease from a previously diagnosed malignancy.

The participant does not have a malignancy with a negligible risk of metastasis or death (eg, 5-year overall survival [OS] ≥90%), such as adequately treated carcinoma in situ of the cervix, non-melanoma skin carcinoma, localized prostate cancer, ductal carcinoma in situ, or Stage I uterine cancer.
The participant has any central nervous system (CNS) lesions, unless definitively treated with CNS-directed local therapy (surgery and/or radiotherapy).
The participant has definitively treated brain metastases and meets the following criteria.
The participant is on a stable dose of ≤10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent for at least >14 days prior to randomization (if requiring steroid treatment).
There is no clinical or radiographic progression in the CNS following CNS-directed definitive radiotherapy and/or surgery.
The time since CNS-directed treatment is ≥28 days prior to randomization.
The participant has a history of leptomeningeal metastasis.
The participant had prior treatment with an anti-PD-L1 agent (where indicated per protocol) within 5 half-lives.
The participant had previous receipt of an MMAE-containing agent or prior docetaxel.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called PF-08046054/SGN-PDL1V Versus Docetaxel in Adult Participants With Previously-Treated Programmed Cell Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1) Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)". Your earlier answers already covered 4 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a biopsy of your lung tumor tested for PD-L1 expression using the 22C3 or SP263 test? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: That I couldn't tell you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been told that your lung cancer has known actionable genetic alterations (AGAs), such as EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 changes? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about those specific genetic changes. I couldn't tell you if I have EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Would you be willing to provide tumor tissue samples for biomarker analysis if needed?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I'm not sure if I can or if they need me to provide more samples.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have any leftover tumor tissue samples from your diagnosis or treatment that were collected within the last 12 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I'm not sure if I have any leftover samples or when they were collected.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have a recent biopsy (within the last 12 months) from a tumor site that was done specifically for this study or diagnosis, if it was medically possible to do?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I'm not sure if I've had a recent biopsy specifically for this study or if it was medically possible.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Regarding your most recent cancer treatment, did your disease progress or return while you were receiving it, or did you stop because of side effects?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: It grew on that treatment. I had Libtayo with carboplatin, and the cancer progressed while I was on it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Did you receive a platinum-based chemotherapy (like carboplatin) along with a PD-(L)1 antibody (like Libtayo) for your metastatic or recurrent cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I had Libtayo with carboplatin.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Was your cancer metastatic or recurrent at that time? Also, did you take Libtayo and carboplatin at the same time, or one after the other?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: It was metastatic, since it had spread to the liver. I took them at the same time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Did your cancer grow or return within 6 months after finishing any prior platinum-based chemotherapy (like carboplatin) given before your current metastatic treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I only had one line of treatment since the cancer became advanced, so I don't have a timeline for prior chemo before that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, did you receive any chemotherapy (like carboplatin) before your cancer spread to the liver, or was the treatment with Libtayo and carboplatin the very first treatment you ever received for your lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: That was the first treatment I had for the advanced cancer. I only had one line of treatment since it became advanced.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any other targeted therapies for your lung cancer besides the Libtayo and carboplatin you mentioned?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any targeted therapies. I only had the Libtayo and carboplatin.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Did you receive any chemotherapy (like carboplatin) specifically to treat your cancer after it had spread (metastatic), or did your cancer return/progress within 6 months of finishing any earlier chemotherapy given before the spread?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I had carboplatin as part of my first and only treatment for the advanced cancer, which was when it had spread to the liver. I don't know about any chemotherapy given before the spread.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with any other type of cancer in the last 3 years, or do you have any remaining signs of a previous cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I had melanoma on my back, but that was removed in 2009. I haven't had any other cancer in the last 3 years.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides the melanoma you mentioned?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, just the melanoma on my back. That was removed in 2009.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with cancer that had spread to your brain, and if so, has that condition been definitively treated?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, the cancer hasn't spread to my brain. The doctor said the lining of my brain and spine is clear.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking prednisone or a similar steroid medication? If so, what is your daily dose?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't take steroid pills like prednisone or dexamethasone every day.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you mentioned your brain and spine lining is clear, have you had any new symptoms like headaches, vision changes, or balance issues since your last scan?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any new headaches, vision changes, or balance issues. My main issue is just that I can't do heavy work anymore.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent scans showing that the cancer in your brain or spine has grown or changed since your last treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, the scans show the cancer is in the liver, not the brain or spine. The doctor said the lining of my brain and spine is clear.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. When was your last treatment specifically for your brain or spine (CNS-directed treatment)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had any treatment for my brain or spine. The cancer is in the liver, and the doctor said the lining of my brain and spine is clear.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received treatment with an anti-PD-L1 medicine (a type of immunotherapy that helps your immune system fight cancer)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I had Libtayo with carboplatin. It grew on that treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received treatment with docetaxel (a chemotherapy medicine) or any medicine containing MMAE?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about docetaxel or MMAE. I haven't had any targeted therapies or antibody-drug conjugates, and I'm not sure about those specific names.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
